account.currentPasswordHint: Required. Being signed in on its own is not enough to change the credential it was minted from.
account.desc: The username and password this server is reached with. Changing either signs out every other device, which is the point: the reason to rotate a credential is that the old one may be known.

agents.approvalTimeoutHint: An unanswered prompt is denied after this. 0 is not allowed.
agents.enabledHint: A disabled agent cannot run a turn and is hidden from the picker.
agents.environmentAllowHint: Comma separated. Each entry is an address (93.184.216.34), a block (10.0.0.0/8), a host name (api.example.com), or a name with a leading dot for its subdomains (.example.com). Nothing inside the environment resolves a name, so a name is reachable over HTTP and HTTPS only.
agents.environmentAlwaysUseOwnHint: Stays in {{environment}} whatever delegates to it. Right for an agent whose image holds the one tool it exists for.
agents.environmentAlwaysUseOwnHostHint: Stays on the host whatever delegates to it, even when the delegating agent runs in a container.
agents.environmentAlwaysUseOwnOffHint: When another agent delegates to this one, the work runs where that agent runs. On its own, it runs in the environment chosen above.
agents.environmentDesc: Choose where this agent's built-in exec tool runs. The host is an environment too: the one commands run in when no definition is named. Installed environments have their own images, hardening, resource limits and network policy.
agents.environmentGatewayProblem: This environment cannot enforce an allow-list: {{why}}
agents.environmentNoProfiles: No environments installed, so commands run on the host. Create one in Settings.
agents.environmentPrivate: Private environment: {{name}}. Each agent and session gets its own instance.
agents.environmentShared: Shared environment: {{name}}. Agents in this workspace asking for the same network reuse one instance.

execRules.desc: Decide per command whether exec runs it, asks first, or refuses. A command no rule matches gets the tool’s own permission.
execRules.empty: No rules yet. Every command gets the tool’s own permission.

error.star: * can only be the last word.

execRules.hint: One argument per word, and a final * matches any remaining arguments. A rule applies wherever the agent runs. The most specific rule wins: more words, then an exact rule, then Deny over Ask over Allow. A wildcard rule on a program that runs other programs, such as env, sudo or python, allows everything.
execRules.shellHint: The most a call to bash, sh or another shell can get. Only a rule naming the exact command decides one on its own. On the host a shell never runs -c.
execRules.title: Command rules

agents.featureToolsDesc: What this agent keeps between sessions, and the instruction sheets it may open.
agents.idHint: Used in links, in the config file, and as the name the model sees when another agent delegates to this one.
agents.idPreview: Will be renamed to “{{id}}”. Delegations and sessions follow; bookmarks and other devices do not.
agents.idTaken: There is already an agent called “{{id}}”.
agents.lazyDiscoveryHint: Every turn normally sends the full schema of every tool, which with many MCP servers can cost thousands of tokens. On, the model is sent only tool_search and the pinned tools. It searches for the rest by name and activates what it needs, once per session.
agents.limitsDesc: The budget a turn runs inside.
agents.maxOutputCharsHint: Longer results are cut head and tail. Also caps how much of a file one read loads.
agents.mcpToolsNote: Contributed by your MCP servers, not by DarkWire. A row marked “not installed” means the tool is not being offered right now: its server may be disconnected, disabled, or no longer configured. The permission is kept either way.
agents.memoryEnabledHint: Off, the agent neither records a memory nor sees the index of what it already knows. The files in memory/ are left alone.
agents.missingNotice: “{{id}}” is no longer configured. This session runs on the default agent until you choose another.
agents.note: Each holds its own prompt, model, permissions and memory. A new one is created as a copy of the default agent’s.
agents.promptAdoptHint: Editing this makes it this agent’s own; until then it follows the built-in and improves with each release. Placeholders:
agents.promptDesc: Everything this agent is told before a session starts. It is yours to rewrite. The workspace jail and the tool approvals are enforced in code and do not read a word of it.
agents.promptLiveHint: Rebuilt every request and never cached, so every line here is paid for five or ten times a turn.
agents.promptMemoryHint: The section that lists what this agent has learned. {{index}} is the generated list. A template without it announces the memory tool and names nothing to use it on.
agents.promptNotPlacedNoMemory: This agent does not have the memory tool, so the section is not placed. Grant it under Tools.
agents.promptNotPlacedNoSkills: This agent does not have the skill tool, so the section is not placed. Grant it under Tools.
agents.promptNotPlacedNoTools: This section isn’t sent to the model. Turn it back on and your wording applies again.
agents.promptOnlySystemHint: Nothing is added around it: no live state or tool-output policy. A template that wants one names its placeholder. A placeholder that changes between requests (the clock, above all) makes the provider re-read the whole prompt each time instead of only the last few lines. That costs more on every request of every turn.
agents.promptPlatformHintDefault: Where this agent’s commands run, and what is there. One default wherever it runs. Describe an environment’s image in its definition and every agent using it inherits that instead.
agents.promptPlatformHintFrom: Where this agent’s commands run, and what is there. The built-in is what this environment’s definition says about its own image, so editing here narrows it for this agent alone and leaves every other agent using that image as it was.
agents.promptRemovedHint: This section is not sent. Restore it to go back to the built-in wording.
agents.promptSkillsHint: The section that lists the workspace’s instruction sheets. {{index}} is the generated catalogue, and it brings its own blank line so a template without it leaves no gap. A sheet’s body is not here. The agent opens the file the catalogue names when it needs one.
agents.promptStray: Nothing will fill {{names}}. It will appear in the prompt exactly as written.
agents.promptSystemHint: The whole first half of the prompt: heading, workspace rules and all.
agents.promptSystemRawHint: Nothing is added around this. A section you want, you name.
agents.promptToolPolicyHint: What makes the delimiters around tool results mean something.
agents.promptToolPolicyUncacheable: Naming {{tag}} here moves this whole section into the part of the prompt that is re-read on every step of a turn. Left out, it is discounted for the life of the session and the live-state section names the delimiter instead.
agents.promptToolPolicyUnfenced: Neither this nor the live-state section names {{tag}} or {{nonce}}. Tool results are still wrapped in the turn’s delimiter, but the model is not told which one, so text inside one can read as an instruction.
agents.promptUncacheable: This template contains something that changes between requests, so the provider re-reads the whole prompt every time rather than only the part after the change. Normally the changing part is a short block at the end and everything above it is discounted.
agents.promptWrapUpHint: Appended to the live state in the last three iterations of a turn.
agents.skillsEnabledHint: Off, the catalogue leaves the prompt and the agent cannot open a sheet. The files in skills/ are left alone.
agents.subagentPromptHint: The tool description the model reads, so it is what decides when the subagent is used. Left empty it uses the sentence shown, which names the agent and follows a rename.
agents.subagentsDesc: Agents this one can hand a task to. Each becomes a tool it can call; the subagent works in its own context and returns a written answer.
agents.subagentsEmpty: No subagents. This agent does all its own work.
agents.subagentsNoneAvailable: There is no other agent to delegate to yet. Create one, and it can be added here.
agents.temperatureHint: Leave empty to send none at all. That is the only thing that works for models that reject it.
agents.title: Agents
agents.toolsDesc: Which tools this agent may call, and what happens when it does. A tool set to Disabled is not offered to the model at all.
agents.toolsEnabledHint: Off sends no tool list at all, for a model that cannot take one. The tools below stay as you set them and come back the moment this agent runs on a model that can call them.
agents.toolsOffNote: These aren’t being sent to the model. Turn it back on and the list applies again.
agents.toolWordingHint: Each box shows the built-in wording until you replace it. This is what decides when the model reaches for the tool.
agents.toolWordingNote: Wording only. Each argument’s type, and whether it is required, come from the tool itself and cannot drift from what it will accept.
agents.visionHint: Off sends an attached image as its file path instead of its contents, for a model that cannot see. The agent can still open it with its file tools.

automation.atHint: Runs once, then unschedules itself. The time is read in {{zone}}.
automation.atUnreal: That is not a real time in this timezone. Clocks skip an hour when daylight saving starts. Pick another.
automation.catchUpHint: A job whose time passed while the server was down runs once when it comes back, not once per missed occurrence.
automation.channelHint: The channel id, such as telegram.
automation.concurrencyHint: How many jobs may run at once. Two keeps a slow job from blocking the queue.
automation.cronFields: A cron expression has five fields.
automation.cronHint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. Read in {{zone}}.
automation.deleteAfterRunHint: How a one-off reminder cleans itself up.
automation.deleteHint: Deletes “{{name}}” and its whole run history. This cannot be undone.
automation.deliverHint: Delivery reaches no channel yet, so results are recorded in your notifications either way.
automation.deliverLabel: Send the result to a channel
automation.deliveryDesc: Where a finished run reports to, once a channel is connected.
automation.enabledHint: A job that is switched off keeps its schedule and does not run.
automation.engineEnabledHint: When this is off, jobs can still be written and none of them fire.
automation.engineTzMoved: The timezone moved to Settings → Account. One zone now reads every schedule and renders every timestamp.
automation.everyHint: Counted from when the previous run finished.
automation.historyDesc: What this job has done, newest first.
automation.kindHeartbeat: Read a task file and decide
automation.messageHint: Sent to the agent as though you had typed it.
automation.modelHint: A cheaper model for the decision. Leave empty to use the agent’s own.
automation.noRuns: This job has not run yet.
automation.note: Each job runs a turn on its own schedule and records what came back. Nothing here needs a browser open.
automation.payloadDesc: What the agent is asked to do when the job fires.
automation.retentionHint: Older runs are dropped as new ones land, along with the sessions they created.
automation.sessionKeyHint: Leave empty to give every run a fresh session. Pinning one is how a job builds up context over time, and how it eventually outgrows the window.
automation.title: Automation
automation.toHint: The channel, user or room to send to.
automation.workspaceHint: Which workspace the run's files are in.
automation.workspacePinned: This job is pinned to a session, so it runs in that session’s workspace and this is ignored.

approval.alwaysHint: Save a rule on this agent that allows commands like this one, then run it.
approval.closed: The approval window closed. The call was refused.
approval.onceHint: Run this one call. The next one asks again.

rule.noMatch: This rule does not cover the command being approved.
rule.patternHint: One argument per word. A final * matches any remaining arguments. Quote an argument that holds a space.
rule.star: * can only be the last word.

approval.sessionHint: Allow this tool for the rest of this session.
approval.sessionHintCommand: Allow this exact command for the rest of this session.
approval.shellWarning: This runs a shell script, which can run any command it contains.

errors.failed: The command did not go through
errors.nothingToBranch: Nothing to branch from: you have not said anything here.
errors.nothingYet: Send a message first. There is no session to act on yet.

errors.usageTemperature: Usage: /temperature <a number from 0 to 2> or /temperature default

notes.effortDefault: {{agent}} now sends no reasoning effort at all. The provider applies its own. Saved.
notes.temperatureDefault: {{agent}} now sends no temperature at all. The provider applies its own. Saved.

commands.stop: Abort the turn that is running

chat.externalImage: External image. Opens in a new tab rather than loading here

noAnswer.reasoningOnly: The model finished its reasoning without writing an answer. Nothing was lost. Regenerating usually produces one.
noAnswer.silent: The model returned nothing at all: no answer, and no tool call. Regenerating usually produces one.

chat.welcomeHint: Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line · / for commands
chat.welcomeNote: The agent reads and writes inside its workspace, and asks before it runs a command or reaches the network. Every tool call shows up in the transcript with its arguments and its output.

common.name: Name
common.notFoundBody: There is nothing at this address.

context.intro: What a turn on this session would send to the model right now.
context.nothingYet: Nothing to measure yet: this session has not started. Send a message and the budget appears here.
context.title: Context

files.conflict: This file changed on disk since it was opened, most likely because the agent wrote to it. Your edits are still here. Reload to take the version on disk and lose them, or copy what you need out first.
files.emptyHint: Drop files anywhere in this box to upload them, or use the Upload button.
files.folderContents_one: Everything inside goes with it: {{count}} item.
files.folderContents_other: Everything inside goes with it: {{count}} items.
files.noMatch_one: Nothing here matches “{{filter}}”. {{count}} entry is hidden.
files.noMatch_other: Nothing here matches “{{filter}}”. {{count}} entries are hidden.
files.notText: This file is not text, so there is nothing to show or edit here. Download it to open it in something that understands it.

files.tooBig: This file is {{size}} and only the first part was read. Saving would delete the rest, so it cannot be edited here. Download it instead.

notifications.clearHint_one: {{count}} notification is deleted, read and unread alike. There is no undo.
notifications.clearHint_other: {{count}} notifications are deleted, read and unread alike. There is no undo.
notifications.empty: Automation runs and expired approvals report themselves here.
notifications.title: Notifications

providers.apiBaseHint: Empty uses the default shown above.
providers.connectionDesc: Where to reach it, and what to open it with. Keys go to the encrypted vault and are never returned by the API.
providers.deleteHint: {{name}} is removed from the settings, and its saved key is deleted with it. Re-adding an endpoint with the same name does not bring the key back.
providers.enabledHint: A disabled endpoint stays configured but is offered to no agent and asked for no models.
providers.identityDesc: What this endpoint is called in the list.
providers.labelHint: Blank uses the provider type’s own name.
providers.loadTypesError: Could not load the provider types: {{message}}
providers.newHint: One endpoint. The type is fixed once it exists. Add the same type twice to run against two servers, and they keep separate keys.
providers.none: No providers yet. Add one, then choose a model on the agent that will use it.
providers.panelDesc: Each row is one endpoint. Add the same type more than once to run against two servers. They keep separate keys, and a key is written to the encrypted vault and never returned by the API.
providers.reachableNoModels: Reachable, though it listed no models.
providers.title: Providers
providers.typeFixedNote: A {{type}} endpoint. The type is fixed for the life of an instance: its saved key is keyed to this id, so talking a different protocol is a different endpoint.
providers.typeHintBase: Defaults to {{base}}, which you can change below.
providers.typeHintNoBase: This type has no default endpoint, so give it one below.
providers.typeHintNone: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works; pick Custom if yours is not listed.

sessions.deleteHint: “{{title}}” and every message in it are removed. There is no undo.
sessions.heading: Latest sessions
sessions.note: Every session in this workspace, including the ones a scheduled job or a subagent started.
sessions.title: Sessions

appearance.languageDesc: What this install speaks. It applies to the web UI and to `darkwire chat` on this server, not only to this browser.
appearance.languageHint: `System` follows your browser until someone chooses otherwise.
appearance.reasoningHint: Applies to the terminal as well as this page.
appearance.themeDesc: Whether the interface is light or dark. This one is yours alone: it is stored in this browser and never written to the config.
appearance.timezoneDesc: The one clock this install uses. Every date and time on screen is shown in it, and a scheduled job is read against it. Changing it moves when existing cron jobs fire.
appearance.timezoneHint: `System` reads your browser’s zone and saves it as a real timezone, so the answer does not change when you open the app somewhere else.
appearance.transcriptDesc: How much of an answer’s working out you see before you ask for it.

channels.accessDesc: The bot answers these Telegram accounts and nobody else. A messaging app has no password on it, so this list is the whole boundary.
channels.adminNotAllowed: {{entry}} is not on the allowlist, so it cannot reach the bot at all.
channels.adminsHint: One id per line. These may change the model and manage workspaces: commands that move the whole install, not only their own session. Leave empty to make everyone above an administrator.
channels.allowlistHint: One per line, as the numeric id or id|label. Message the bot and read the server log to find your own. A negative id is a group, and inside one both the group and the person typing must be listed.
channels.allowlistRequired: Add at least one account, or the bot would answer nobody.
channels.badId: {{entry}} is not a Telegram id. Use the number, optionally as id|label.
channels.enabledHint: Connects the bot when the server has a token for it.
channels.telegramDesc: Talk to the same agent from a phone. A Telegram turn runs on this install, in the sessions the sidebar lists.
channels.tokenHint: From @BotFather. Stored in the encrypted vault, and never sent back to this page.
channels.tokenReplaceHint: A token is saved. Type to replace it, or clear this field and save to remove it.

environments.advancedHint: Runtime, identity and hardening. The defaults are the hardened shape, and weakening one is reported on the list rather than refused.
environments.capsAddHint: One per line. NET_ADMIN, SYS_ADMIN and SYS_MODULE are never granted.
environments.capsDropHint: One per line. ALL is dropped in code whatever this says.
environments.deleteHint: Agents naming “{{name}}” will refuse their next turn until you point them somewhere else. Containers already running from it are swept when they go idle.
environments.devicesHint: One per line. A host device is reachable from inside the container.
environments.envHint: One host variable name per line. Values are never stored here.
environments.identityDesc: What this environment is called, and what runs in it.
environments.imageHint: Type a tag such as node:22 and press Resolve, or paste a digest. A definition pins a digest because a tag can be repointed later, which would leave it running an image nobody chose.
environments.installedDescription: The environments an agent may select. Each one is a definition file under the policy directory, created and edited here. An agent with none named runs on the host.
environments.nameHint: Lower case, digits and dashes. It is the filename, and it cannot be changed later.
environments.nameInvalid: Use lower case letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or digit.
environments.nameTaken: An environment of this name is already installed.
environments.noneInstalled: No environments installed, so every agent runs its commands on the host. Create one in Settings.
environments.noNewPrivilegesHint: Stops a setuid binary gaining more than the process started with.
environments.numberInvalid: Enter a number of zero or more.
environments.promptHeading: Leave the heading out. This is placed under one, so a second reads as a section inside a section.
environments.promptHint: Told to every agent that runs here, in place of the default Running commands wording. Say what is installed, which shell, and what is not there. An agent can override it.
environments.promptPlaceholder:
Alpine 3.23. git, util-linux and ca-certificates are installed.
The shell is ash, not bash: no arrays and no [[ ]].
environments.readOnlyRootHint: Everything outside the writable mounts below is read-only.
environments.resolvedLocal: “{{reference}}” was already here. The digest is above.
environments.resolvedPulled: “{{reference}}” was pulled. The digest is above.
environments.resourcesDesc: What one container may spend. Zero means no limit.
environments.runningDescription: Stopping one is safe. The next command starts a fresh one.
environments.runtimeHint: runc is the engine default. runsc and kata need their own install.
environments.seccompHint: unconfined lets a container call any syscall the kernel offers.
environments.startHint: Warms a container from “{{name}}” now, instead of waiting for a tool to need one.
environments.tmpfsHint: One mount per line, such as /tmp:rw,nosuid,size=64m.
environments.userHint: uid:gid inside the container. An allow-listed egress refuses root.
environments.workdirHint: Where the workspace is mounted. Absolute, and never the root.

extensions.approveHint: An extension runs inside the server, with the access the server has. Approving records a digest of the files it holds right now. Editing any of them withdraws this approval automatically.
extensions.description: Directories under ~/.darkwire/extensions. Each one has to be approved before anything in it runs.
extensions.none: No extensions installed. Put a directory holding a darkwire.extension.json under ~/.darkwire/extensions, then approve it here.
extensions.title: Extensions

mcp.authDesc: For a server that wants an OAuth token rather than a header.
mcp.clientIdHint: Leave as issued if the server registers clients dynamically.
mcp.commandHint: The program to run, for example npx or uvx.
mcp.deleteHint: “{{name}}” will be disconnected and its tools will stop being offered to any agent.
mcp.description: Tool servers this install connects to. Their tools appear beside the built-ins, and each agent decides for itself which of them it may call.
mcp.enabledHint: Off keeps the settings and stops connecting.
mcp.enabledToolsHint: One name per line, as the server calls them. A trailing * matches a prefix. Empty means every tool it offers.
mcp.envHint: NAME=value, one per line. The child inherits nothing else.
mcp.exposureDesc: Which of this server’s tools this install advertises at all.
mcp.headersHint: Name: value, one per line. These are stored in config.yaml in the clear. Use OAuth below for anything that should not be.
mcp.loadError: The settings could not be loaded: {{message}}
mcp.none: No MCP servers yet. Add one to give your agents tools this install does not ship.
mcp.noSuchServer: There is no MCP server called “{{id}}”.
mcp.serverIdHint: Used in every tool name this server contributes, and fixed once saved: renaming it would revoke its tools from every agent holding one.
mcp.title: MCP servers
mcp.toolTimeoutHint: 0 waits as long as the server takes.
mcp.transportHint: A local command, or a URL. Streamable HTTP is what most remote servers speak; SSE is the older one.
mcp.urlScheme: Must start with http:// or https://
mcp.usesOAuthHint: Tokens are written to the credential vault, never to config.yaml.

tools.cacheEntriesHint: Pages and result sets held in memory. 0 turns the cache off.
tools.cacheTtlHint: Seconds an entry stays usable. 0 turns the cache off.
tools.egressElsewhere: What an agent may reach is on the agent, under Network, because it is a statement about that agent rather than about this machine.
tools.maxDownloadKbHint: Kilobytes, counted as the body arrives and after it is decompressed. This bounds what a page can do to memory, not what reaches the model: how much text the model sees is the agent's result budget.
tools.readTimeoutHint: Seconds per page read inside a search, so one slow site cannot eat the batch.
tools.searchProviderHint: Built in scrapes public search front doors and falls back to Hacker News. It needs no setup and will break without warning, because those pages change and rate-limit a server address. A SearXNG instance you run is the configuration that holds.
tools.searchUrlHint: The base URL of your instance, for example https://searx.example.com. The instance must have the JSON format enabled.
tools.searchUrlRequired: A SearXNG instance needs a URL.
tools.timeoutHint: Seconds to wait for one page.
tools.userAgentHint: Leave empty to send the browser profile shown here, which is what gets past most bot walls. A value is sent verbatim and identifies this install, with the browser client hints dropped so the two cannot contradict each other.
tools.webDesc: One answer per install: which backend answers a search, how this install identifies itself, and what every request is bounded by.

setup.apiBaseHint: Empty uses the default shown above.
setup.asking: Asking the provider what it has…
setup.codeNote: It was printed in the terminal that started this server. It works once.

workspaces.filter: Filter workspaces by name or folder

workspaces.folderHint: The directory created in the workspaces folder. Leave it blank to use the one derived from the name.

workspaces.folderReserved: That folder name is reserved and cannot name a workspace.
workspaces.folderShape: Use 1–40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
workspaces.folderTaken: A workspace already uses that folder.
workspaces.identityDesc: What this workspace is called, and where its files are.
workspaces.missingNotice: “{{id}}” is no longer listed. This session still runs in it until you choose another.
workspaces.namedNote_one: Isolated from every other workspace: it cannot reach their files, and they cannot reach its. {{count}} session runs in it, last updated {{updated}}.
workspaces.namedNote_other: Isolated from every other workspace: it cannot reach their files, and they cannot reach its. {{count}} sessions run in it, last updated {{updated}}.
workspaces.nameHint: A label. Changing it moves nothing on disk and breaks no link.
workspaces.newHint: A name, and the folder it gets in the workspaces directory. Neither is a path, and the two are independent: the folder only starts out derived from the name.
workspaces.note: A workspace is a folder the agent works in. Each one is its own folder and none of them can reach another's files.
workspaces.title: Workspaces
